title: Greenfield Three.js + Vite TypeScript scene
request: Create a responsive interactive Three.js scene in a Vite TypeScript application.
doneWhen: Current stable Three.js metadata and the exact APIs used are verified from authoritative sources.
The canvas follows its container, updates camera/renderer sizing, and handles high-DPI without an unconditional maximum DPR assumption.
There is one animation loop and teardown disposes listeners and owned GPU resources.
Typecheck/build/tests pass and the production build loads without console or asset errors.

title: Add React Three Fiber and Drei to an existing React application
request: Add a reusable 3D product component to an existing React application using R3F/Drei.
doneWhen: Installed React major is discovered before selecting Fiber/Drei versions and current peer compatibility is verified.
The scene uses R3F's render lifecycle rather than a duplicate requestAnimationFrame loop.
Canvas sizing, suspense/loading/error behavior, and component teardown fit the existing application.
The existing application's typecheck, tests, lint, build, and representative responsive interaction checks pass.

title: Safely upgrade an existing 3D dependency stack
request: Upgrade Three.js, R3F/Drei, engine wrappers, or related 3D packages without breaking the application.
doneWhen: The existing manifest/lockfile and exact installed/ranged versions are recorded before changes.
Registry stable versions, peer dependencies, engine requirements, and official migration/API changes are verified.
The upgrade is minimal and any required API migration is scoped to affected code rather than unrelated refactoring.
Tests/typecheck/lint/build plus original 3D user flows pass, and the lockfile contains no unintended dependency drift.

title: Production glTF/GLB asset loading and optimization
request: Load and optimize production glTF assets with optional Meshopt/Draco/KTX2-style compression.
doneWhen: The engine loader and every requested glTF extension/decoder path are verified against current official docs and Khronos glTF.
Build-time transformations use current glTF Transform APIs/CLI where appropriate and original source assets remain recoverable.
Production output serves model, texture, decoder, and worker assets from correct URLs/MIME types.
Visual/animation fidelity is checked after optimization and failure/loading states are handled without silent scene corruption.

title: WebGPU rendering with a supported fallback
request: Use WebGPU when supported while retaining a functional WebGL path for the product's required browsers.
doneWhen: Current WebGPU browser status and the selected engine's exact WebGPU initialization API are verified.
Capability detection happens before selecting the backend and secure-context/deployment requirements are satisfied.
Unsupported or failed WebGPU initialization reaches the defined WebGL/fallback experience rather than a blank canvas.
Both available backends are smoke-tested for rendering, resize, assets, teardown, and console/runtime errors.

title: Add Rapier physics to a browser 3D application
request: Add deterministic-feeling rigid-body physics with Rapier to a Three.js or R3F application.
doneWhen: The normal Rapier WASM package is preferred unless verified bundler/runtime limitations justify the compat package.
Async WASM initialization completes before world use and simulation stepping has a deliberate fixed/variable timestep strategy.
Visual transforms and physics transforms have one explicit synchronization direction and teardown releases the physics world/resources.
Build and runtime smoke tests exercise collision, pause/remount/route behavior, and the targeted browser environment.

title: Babylon.js product viewer or interactive application
request: Build or extend a Babylon.js viewer with glTF loading, camera controls, and production packaging.
doneWhen: Current scoped Babylon.js ES-module packages and APIs are verified; legacy UMD packages are not chosen for a new bundled app without a reason.
Only required engine/features/loaders are imported and asset/plugin registration is explicit.
Engine resize/render lifecycle and scene/engine disposal are wired to application lifecycle.
Production build, model loading, controls, resize, and console/runtime behavior are verified.

title: PlayCanvas browser game or interactive 3D application
request: Create or modernize a PlayCanvas Engine application with WebGPU/WebGL2-aware rendering.
doneWhen: The current PlayCanvas package/API and supported graphics devices are verified from official sources.
The application initializes the requested graphics backend with capability-aware fallback consistent with product support targets.
Entities/components/assets and application lifecycle use current engine APIs without mixing obsolete examples.
Build and representative browser/device smoke tests cover rendering, input, resize, asset load, and teardown.

title: CesiumJS globe, terrain, and 3D Tiles application
request: Build a CesiumJS geospatial experience with terrain/3D Tiles and production bundling.
doneWhen: Current CesiumJS package/setup guidance is verified before configuring the bundler.
CESIUM_BASE_URL/static Workers, ThirdParty, Assets, and Widgets are correctly served or handled by a verified integration and CSS is included as needed.
Tokens/credentials follow the service's intended client/server scope and no unrelated secret is shipped to the browser.
Production build loads required workers/assets/terrain/tiles, resizes correctly, and destroys owned viewers/resources on teardown.

title: WebXR immersive VR/AR experience
request: Add an immersive WebXR mode to an existing web 3D scene.
doneWhen: Current W3C WebXR semantics and the selected engine's integration API are verified instead of relying on old tutorials.
Secure context, navigator/session support, user activation, required/optional features, and session-end behavior are handled.
A non-XR path remains usable when the product requires access on devices without the requested XR mode.
The experience is tested on representative supported XR hardware/browser when available, with environment limitations stated when not available.

title: Diagnose mobile GPU crashes, stutter, or memory leaks
request: Find and fix a 3D experience that becomes slow, loses context, or crashes on mobile/high-DPI devices.
doneWhen: The failure is reproduced or instrumented before optimization and console/context-loss evidence is captured.
Resolution/DPR, draw calls, texture formats/sizes, geometry, render targets, post-processing, asset lifetime, and per-frame allocations are measured rather than guessed.
Fixes preserve visual requirements while removing verified bottlenecks/leaks and dispose owned resources on navigation/reload.
The original failing device class plus desktop regression targets are exercised after the change.

title: 3D inside SSR or hybrid rendering frameworks
request: Integrate a Three.js/R3F/engine canvas into an SSR or hybrid-rendered application without server crashes or hydration problems.
doneWhen: The framework's current client boundary/dynamic-loading mechanism is verified from its official docs before code is written.
DOM/WebGL/WebGPU/WebXR initialization cannot execute on the server and the render target exists before engine creation.
Loading/layout avoids hydration-size mismatches and route/remount behavior cleans up all owned render resources/listeners.
Server build, client hydration/navigation, production build, and representative responsive scene interaction all pass.
